ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.12 Ryde voucher (metered excess-distance value of the single unexempted off-route segment) to the rider; no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride: $44.82 total with a distance component of $29.44 over 20.88 km [F8], so the meter's per-km rate is $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km, the same rate the fare record uses to bill 5.29 km of excess as $7.46 [F5]. Under RD-2 the refund measure for a RydeTAXI detour is the extra_km of the unexempted off-route segments times that rate, and the corridor/matching margin not captured in any segment is expressly left with the driver.

There is exactly one off-route segment: 14:33–14:48, 7.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.40 km, adding 5.05 km and peaking 1987 m from the optimal route [F4]. The overall excess of 5.3 km (+34%) and the 38.5-minute duration against a 21.7-minute estimate corroborate that magnitude [F1][F3].

That segment is not exempt. The rider's message was a general authorisation — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F10], sent at 14:30, before the segment began at 14:33 [F4]. Read in context against the driver's own offer at 14:29 to "take another way" [F9], it covers the routing chosen to get to VivoCity, but RD-5's general-authorisation category does not cover an errand of the driver's own. The driver's statement admits exactly that: "I went round the jam and stopped briefly to collect something on the way" [F12]. The car stood still 4 min 0 s at 14:38–14:42, 7443 m from the pickup and 6033 m from the drop-off — a mid-trip stop inside the off-route window [F2] — and no rider message asked for any stop, the chat record being complete at two timestamped messages [F11]. RD-3(a) therefore gives no cover: the rider named no place, so the driver's choice of stopping point cannot be excused, and the whole way to a stop that was not the rider's named destination remains within the deviation (RD-3(b)). The driver's claim in F12 that "the rider said any route was fine" is a post-trip assertion, not rider consent before the segment, and cannot establish agreement under RD-5 read with G11; the full segment therefore counts.

No traffic exemption is available: the trace settles that no qualifying incident existed on the replaced stretch, and F16 confirms no traffic incident near the route during the trip window [F16]. The Central Expressway speed band 2 reading (10–19 km/h, 14:11–14:33) [F13] is corroborative only under RD-4(b) and does not exempt a segment by itself, while the alternative roads ran at band 4 [F14][F15]; fair weather does not help [F17]. The segment accordingly stands unexempted under RD-1.

Amount: 5.05 km × $1.4100/km = $7.1205, rounded to $7.12 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. I use the segment's measured extra_km (F4) rather than the billed 5.29 km in F5, so the 0.24 km corridor/matching remainder stays with the driver as RD-2 prescribes; the trace's formula is extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km.

The meter's waiting line of $1.15 (4.4 min × $0.26/min) [F6] is not refundable: on a RydeTAXI, stop duration is charged as meter waiting units per RD-3(c), and the rider's "meter was way above the estimate" complaint does not reach it. No ERP/toll top-up is possible — the fare data carries no such field [F8][FARE-2].

No account flag attaches. RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days; the driver's profile records 4 disputes and 2 upheld but 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days [F19], and the rider has none [F18], so the "repeated" precondition is unmet. Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" is a route instruction, the driver's warning about the jam and his offer of another way [F9] and his admission about the stop [F12] contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the complaint is about the fare [F11]; safety_concern is none. The record settles every element the ruling needs, so evidence is sufficient.

The driver's own statement [F12] admits he 'stopped briefly to collect something on the way', and the car stood still 4 min 0 s at 14:38–14:42, 7443 m from pickup and 6033 m from drop-off [F2], with no rider request for any stop in the complete two-message chat record [F11]; RD-3(a) therefore gives no cover because the rider named no place. rejected_claims.reason: Partly rejected as to outcome only: the segment exists as an off-route deviation [F4] but its legal effect is not RD-1 alone — RD-2's RydeTAXI branch limits the remedy to the metered distance value of the unexempted segment, which is $7.12, not the whole billed excess of $7.46 [F5][F8].
Accepted in substance and granted: 5.05 km (F4) × $1.4100/km ($29.44 ÷ 20.88 km, F8) = $7.12 under RD-2; the rider's narrower figure is the correct segment measure, so this claim is not rejected.

Rejected: the general authorisation in F10 does not exempt the 14:33–14:48 segment under RD-5, because the record — the driver's own admission in F12 and the unexplained 4-minute halt at F2 — places part of the segment on the driver's private errand, which a general route permission does not cover.

Rejected: RD-4 requires a qualifying incident on the replaced optimal stretch, and the trace plus F16 show none; a band-2 speed record (F13) is corroborative only under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt the segment, and the alternative roads ran at band 4 (F14, F15).

Rejected: although the halt produced no separate segment and standing time is not itself refundable under RD-2, the halt disqualifies the whole 14:33–14:48 segment from RD-5/ RD-3(a) exemption [F2][F12], so the segment's excess kilometres are refundable rather than limited to a mere ceiling of the billed $7.46.

Rejected as to quantum: RD-2 measures the refund by the segment's extra_km (5.05 km, F4) × the per-km rate, i.e. $7.12; the billed 5.29 km/$7.46 (F5) is the collected amount, and the 0.24 km corridor/matching difference is the portion RD-2 leaves with the driver.
Accepted: the $1.15 metered waiting line (F6) is not refundable on a RydeTAXI under RD-3(c), so the driver succeeds on this item.

Rejected: RD-6's precondition route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is unmet — F19 records 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days (and F18 none for the rider) — so no flag_account attaches, and the profile may not be used to decide the case.
